t: You're at the site of St Christopher le Stocks, which was a parish church on the north side of Threadneedle Street, in Broad Street Ward. It was of medieval origin and was rebuilt after the Great Fire of London in 1666 by Sir Christopher Wren. In 1781 it was demolished to make way for an extension of the neighbouring Bank of England. Wren was responsible for rebuilding fifty-two City churches after the fire, and he is also known for St Paul's Cathedral, completed in 1710. So the church is gone, but the Bank of England now stands in its place.
